title: Which do you prefer - usage based or subscription pricing?
author: spacespacespapce

replies.author: spacespacespapce
replies.body:
Local was my first goal but OSS models take too many iterations and lead to more errors in Blender. 


Something like kimi-k2 could work but the agent requires so many steps that it just won't be usable imo

comments.author: GaiusVictor
comments.body: Is this a service you're providing? If that's your service, then I prefer usage-based, but the best business practice imo is to always provide both options, but subscription being a tad cheaper than usage-based for that same amount of use.

replies.author: spacespacespapce
replies.body:

Okay I'll think about how to implement both thanks for your suggestions.

comments.author: Denaton_
comments.body: I have the computer to run stuff locally so i perfer that..

comments.author: spacespacespapce
comments.body:
Hey all, I'm working on a tool for editable AI 3D assets in Blender, and I’m hitting a wall on how to charge for it fairly.


From a developer standpoint, what makes more sense to you? Would you prefer a low monthly subscription that gives you a fixed number of credits/builds? Or would you rather go fully usage-based, where you pay per model generated but have no recurring fees? 


Trying to figure out which model feels less predatory and more supportive of indie dev workflows.  Thoughts?
